messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: High 5xx rate on inference-api (canary) - 17% error rate over 2m, routing ~10% traffic to canary. Auto-escalation: paged oncall.
maya: I'm on it, starting investigation. grabbing canary logs and deployment status.
maya: kubectl get pods -n prod | grep inference-canary
maya: pod inference-canary-7f8bb9 Restarts: 24 CrashLoopBackOff
maya: checking events and liveness failures
lee: I see repeated OOMKilled in pod logs, plus readiness probe failing on /healthz
sam: HPA scaled target down to 1 because minReplicas was accidentally set to 1 in the canary manifest (should be 3). looks like traffic spike + low replicas -> OOMs and queueing
jess-oncall: what's customer impact? Any external 5xx spikes reaching customers?
maya: initial impact: ~6% of production requests are routed to canary (traffic split) and 17% of those erroring, overall ~1% of total requests 5xx. Some customers hitting inference timeouts; support ticket #INC-987 raised.
carter: can we flip traffic back to stable? Set routing to 0% for canary now.
lee: doing routing rollback in router:PATCH /routes/inference - setting canary_weight=0
lee: router change applied, verifying.
incident-bot: Router update: canary_weight -> 0 (applied) :white_check_mark:
maya: requests to canary have dropped to ~0%, error rate on stable back to baseline. Good.
sam: we still need to address why pods are stuck restarting and failing drains when we attempt to cordon/evict node for remediation.
maya: attempted node drain of node-gpu-07 to reprovision kernel headers. drain hung: "error: unable to evict pods due to PDB". There is a PodDisruptionBudget blocking eviction: inference-stable PDB minAvailable=80%.
carter: that PDB is too strict for small cluster size. Oncall, can you temporarily override eviction policy to allow drain? Risky for stability but we need node fixed.
jess-oncall: I'm hesitant. Let's try restart of container process inside pod first to avoid full node drain. maya - any chance of graceful restart?
maya: tried kubectl exec -> system restart of worker process, but not stable; container memory growth resumes and OOMs occur.
lee: new hypothesis: a library change in the canary image toggled a new batcher which defaults to aggressive prefetch -> memory spike. The canary manifest also had a bad env override: BATCH_PREFETCH=64 instead of 6.
sam: that explains combo: low replicas + aggressive batching -> OOMs.
carter: mitigation plan:
1) feature flag kill-switch to disable canary feature (we already routed traffic to 0%)
2) roll back canary deployment image to previous stable image tag
3) update manifest to correct minReplicas and BATCH_PREFETCH
4) cordon+drain node after PDB adjustment or manual eviction
jess-oncall: I'll flip kill-switch in LaunchDarkly now and request rollback for the image. tagging @eng-releases to approve immediate rollback.
jess-oncall: LD flag rollout_new_batcher -> OFF :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Feature flag change recorded: rollout_new_batcher OFF by jess-oncall at 2931414255
lee: opening rollback PR with revert to image redwood/inference:2026-03-07-stable -> deploying.
sam: applying manifest patch to set canary minReplicas=3 and BATCH_PREFETCH=6, but we'll hold that until we validate the image rollback.
maya: rollback deployment applied; pods are starting with stable image. Observed older entrypoint and no batcher logs.
maya: monitoring memory usage on the nodes - stabilized. no new OOMKilled in last 30s.
carter: regarding PDB, I propose we patch PDB minAvailable -> 1 temporarily to allow node maintenance, then revert after.
jess-oncall: do it, but coordinate with SRE to ensure we're not causing mass disruption.
lee: patching PDB: kubectl patch pdb inference-stable-pdb -n prod -p '{"spec":{"minAvailable":1}}'
lee: patch applied. Proceeding to drain node-gpu-07.
maya: drain now completed, node reprovisioned and returned to pool.
sre-bot: post-action checklist triggered: run cluster e2e smoke, check autoscaler events, validate HPA configs.
sam: HPA misconfig root cause: canary manifest had targetCPUUtilizationPercentage 90 and minReplicas 1 — mismatch for spikey workloads. Adding an enforced PR check to prevent minReplicas < 2 for inference deployments.
jess-oncall: customer impact summary: small subset of customers (~5-7 individual sessions) saw 502s/timeout; no data loss. Support notified those customers proactively. Severity: Sev2 (partial service degradation).
carter: timeline notes for postmortem: - 2931414000 alert triggered; - 2931414102 routing rollback to 0% - 2931414255 flag OFF - 2931414320 image rollback started - 2931414480 node drain & reprovision completed - 2931415000 monitoring stable
maya: handoff to next oncall (sam) in 30m for follow-up and postmortem writeup. Sam, please pick up the action items: update manifests, add CI check, PDB default change, and confirm stable cluster overnight.
sam: taking handoff. I'll lead the postmortem and set mitigation PRs. Sending notes to #postmortems.
jess-oncall: tl;dr: aggressive batcher + wrong minReplicas + routing -> canary OOMs. Immediate mitigations: route->0, flag off, image rollback, fix manifests, patch PDB, drain node. :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks team. creating follow-up tickets: INF-2345 (manifest fixes), INF-2346 (CI gating), INF-2347 (PDB policy). Assigning owners.
incident-bot: Incident closed for now. If error rate climbs again, this thread will auto-escalate. :lock_with_ink_pen:
jen: (bot) Please add any lingering notes; otherwise I'll mark for postmortem draft generation.
sam: I'll upload logs and a short triage in #postmortems within 2 hours.
maya: adding relevant logs snippet:
```
2026-03-14T01:04:12Z inference-canary-7f8bb9 - OOMKilled: rss=3.4GiB limit=2GiB
2026-03-14T01:04:12Z worker: batcher init prefetch=64
2026-03-14T01:04:13Z readiness probe failing: GET /healthz 500
```
maya: closing my loop, handing off to sam. :slightly_smiling_face:
